25531-representative-plays-by-american-d.title: Representative Plays By American Dramatists 1856 1911 The Mo
25531-representative-plays-by-american-d.creator: Unknown
25531-representative-plays-by-american-d.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. I have seen Clyde Fitch on many diverse occasions. Through incisive comment on people, contemporary manners, and plays, which was let drop in conversation, I was able to estimate the natural tendency of Fitch's mind. His interest was never concerned solely with dominant characters; he was quick rather to sense the idiosyncrasies of the average person.

arxiv-1904-07169.title: Wajsberg algebras arising from binary block codes
arxiv-1904-07169.creator: Cristina FLAUT and Radu VASILE
arxiv-1904-07169.description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper we presented some connections between BCK-commutative bounded algebras, MV-algebras, Wajsberg algebras and binary block codes. Using connections between these three algebras, we will associate to each of them a binary block code and, in some circumstances, we will prove that the converse is also true. Keywords: BCK bounded commutative algebras, MV-algebras, Wajsberg algebras, block codes.

arxiv-2304-14452.title: Mind the Gap I: H α \alpha Activity of M Dwarfs Near the Partially/Fully Convective Boundary and a New H α \alpha Emission Deficiency Zone on the Main Sequence Journal: AJ Facilities: CTIO:1.5m (CHIRON) Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , NumPy ( Van der Walt, Colbert & Varoquaux 2011 ) , astropy ( Astropy
arxiv-2304-14452.creator: Wei-Chun Jao, Todd J. Henry, Russel J. White, Azmain H. Nisak, Hodari-Sadiki Hubbard-James, Leonardo A. Paredes, Vanders B. Lewis, Jr
arxiv-2304-14452.description: Abstract Since identifying the gap in the H-R Diagram (HRD) marking the transition between partially and fully convective interiors, a unique type of slowly pulsating M dwarf has been proposed. These unstable M dwarfs provide new laboratories in which to understand how changing interior structures can produce potentially observable activity at the surface.

arxiv-2405-02246.title: What matters when building vision-language models?
arxiv-2405-02246.creator: Hugo Laurençon, Léo Tronchon, Matthieu Cord, Victor Sanh * The order was chosen randomly
arxiv-2405-02246.description: Abstract The growing interest in vision-language models (VLMs) has been driven by improvements in large language models and vision transformers. Despite the abundance of literature on this subject, we observe that critical decisions regarding the design of VLMs are often not justified.

arxiv-2412-05324.title: Residual Growth Control for General Maps and an Approximate Inverse Function Result
arxiv-2412-05324.creator: Mario Amrein
arxiv-2412-05324.description: Abstract . The need to control the residual of a potentially nonlinear function ℱ \mathcal{F} arises in several situations in mathematics. For example, computing the zeros of a given map, or the reduction of some cost function during an optimization process are such situations.

arxiv-2503-17773.title: Note on a certain category of mod p p representations
arxiv-2503-17773.creator: Reinier Sorgdrager
arxiv-2503-17773.description: Abstract Let p > 3 p>3 be a prime number, f ≥ 1 f\geq 1 an integer. We consider a certain full subcategory 𝒞 \mathcal{C} of the category of smooth admissible mod p p representations of either GL 2 ⁡ 𝐐 p f \GL_{2}\mathbf{Q}_{p^{f}} or of the group of units of the quaternion algebra over 𝐐 p f \mathbf{Q}_{p^{f}} .

arxiv-2506-07548.title: Curriculum Learning With Counterfactual Group Relative Policy Advantage For Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Thanks: This research was conducted during W. Jin’s visit to the University of Hong Kong (HKU). (Corresponding author: H. Du) Thanks: W. Jin is with the School of Information and Communicat
arxiv-2506-07548.creator: Weiqiang Jin, Hongyang Du, Guizhong Liu
arxiv-2506-07548.description: Abstract Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has achieved strong performance in cooperative adversarial tasks. However, most existing methods typically train agents against fixed opponent strategies and rely on such meta-static difficulty conditions, which limits their adaptability to changing environments and often leads to suboptimal policies.

arxiv-2602-21107.title: Resilient Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks Thanks: This work was supported by the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme (grant agreement No. 101001331) and by a research grant from the Department for the Economy Northern Ireland unde
arxiv-2602-21107.creator: Junbin Yu, Tianyu Lu, Mohammadali Mohammadi, and Michail Matthaiou
arxiv-2602-21107.description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel optimization framework for enhancing the security resilience of cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) networks with multi-antenna access points (APs) and protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) under active eavesdropping. Based on the main principles of absorption, adaptation, and recovery, we formulate a security-aware resilience metric to quantify the system performance during and after a security outage.

pmc-10609774.title: Development, Characterization and Pharmacological Evaluation of Cannabidiol-Loaded Long Circulating Niosomes
pmc-10609774.creator: Viliana Gugleva, Katerina Ahchiyska, Dilyana Georgieva, Rositsa Mihaylova, Spiro Konstantinov, Erik Dimitrov, Natalia Toncheva-Moncheva, Stanislav Rangelov, Aleksander Forys, Barbara Trzebicka, Denitsa Momekova, Ana Cazacu, Elena-Laura Ursu
pmc-10609774.description: Cannabidiol (CBD) is a promising drug candidate with pleiotropic pharmacological activity, whose low aqueous solubility and unfavorable pharmacokinetics have presented obstacles to its full clinical implementation. The rational design of nanocarriers, including niosomes for CBD encapsulation, can provide a plausible approach to overcoming these limitations.

pmc-10709856.title: Genes polymorphism as risk factor of recurrent urolithiasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-10709856.creator: Nur Rasyid, Soefiannagoya Soedarman
pmc-10709856.description: IntroductionUrolithiasis is one of the most prevalent diseases worldwide. Its prevalence is rising, both in developing and developed countries. It is known that genetic factors play big roles in the development of urolithiasis. One of the suspected factors is gene polymorphism.

pmc-10738889.title: RESILIENCE IN JAPANESE OLDER IMMIGRANTS AND ROLES OF COMMUNITY SUPPORT DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
pmc-10738889.creator: Mineko Wada, Sarah Canham
pmc-10738889.description: The objective of this community-based study was to explore how Japanese older immigrants cultivated resilience in overcoming challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic and how Tonari Gumi, a community service agency, supported the process. As Japanese people make up a small proportion of the population in Canada, there are limited resources to meet their distinct needs.

pmc-11713371.title: Variational autoencoder latent space as a robust and pragmatic clinical classification tool for dementia
pmc-11713371.creator: William C Wakefield, Leland R Barnard, Hugo Botha, Jonathan Graff‐Radford, Kejal Kantarci, Brad F Boeve, Ronald C Petersen, Clifford R Jack, Val J Lowe, David T Jones
pmc-11713371.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMany proposed clinical decision support systems (CDSS) require multiple disparate data elements as input, which makes implementation difficult, and furthermore have a black‐box nature leading to low interpretability. Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography (FDG‐PET) is an established modality for the diagnosis of dementia, and a CDSS that uses only an FDG‐PET image to produce a reliable and understandable result would ease both of these challenges to clinical application.MethodA deep variational autoencoder (VAE) was used to extract a latent representation of each image through

pmc-12001349.title: Identifying serious underlying diagnoses among patients with brief resolved unexplained events (BRUEs): a Canadian cohort study
pmc-12001349.creator: Nassr Nama, Zerlyn Lee, Kara Picco, Falla Jin, Jeffrey N Bone, Julie Quet, Jessica Foulds, Josée Anne Gagnon, Chris Novak, Brigitte Parisien, Matthew Donlan, Ran D Goldman, Anupam Sehgal, Ronik Kanani, Joanna Holland, Polina Kyrychenko, Nardin Kirolos, Ioulia Opotchanova, Émilie Harnois, Alyse Schac
pmc-12001349.description: ABSTRACTObjectiveTo describe the demographics and clinical outcomes of infants with brief resolved unexplained events (BRUE).DesignA retrospective cohort study.Setting11 centres within the Canadian Paediatric Inpatient Research Network.PatientsPatients presenting to the emergency department (ED) following a BRUE (2017–2021) were eligible, when no clinical cause identified after a thorough history and physical examination.

pmc-12515695.title: Sepsis‐Induced Anti‐Amphiphysin Antibody‐Associated Paraneoplastic Syndrome: A Case Report
pmc-12515695.creator: Dexin Min, Meng Yuan, Chenda Feng, Wenjing Tang, Lichao Sun
pmc-12515695.description: Sepsis is a severe systemic response to infection that can induce a variety of complications, including paraneoplastic syndrome (PNS). Anti‐amphiphysin antibody‐associated PNS is a rare autoimmune disorder associated with tumors. We review the case of a 27‐year‐old man who presented with a 3‐day history of fever, disturbance of consciousness, and oliguria.

pmc-12584943.title: Municipal Governments' Long‐Term Care Prevention Efforts and Homebound Status of Older Adults: A Three‐Year Cohort Study in Japan
pmc-12584943.creator: Duc Sy Minh Ho, Kaori Yamaguchi, Kazushige Ide, Sakura Kiuchi, Naoki Kondo, Jun Aida
pmc-12584943.description: AimHomebound status poses considerable risks for adverse health outcomes among older adults. To enhance the comprehensive care system, municipalities have implemented efforts aimed at long‐term care prevention. It is assumed that such efforts may help mitigate homeboundness. Therefore, this study examined the association between municipal long‐term care prevention efforts and homebound status among older adults.

pmc-12656729.title: Two Decades of Change: Evolving Maternal Characteristics and Perinatal Outcomes in Pregnant Women Living with HIV
pmc-12656729.creator: Laura Salazar, Anna Goncé, Isabel Matas, Judit Balcells, Laura García-Otero, Clàudia Fortuny, Berta Torres, Ana González-Cordón, Montse Palacio, Eduard Gratacós, Francesc Figueras, Fatima Crispi, Marta López, Steven L Zeichner
pmc-12656729.description: Implementation of universal antiretroviral treatment (ART) in pregnancy has improved maternal health and reduced vertical transmission. However, women living with HIV (WLHIV) still experience worse perinatal outcomes. This retrospective study compared demographic, virological factors, ART regimens and perinatal outcomes in pregnant WLHIV between 2000–2010 (n = 318) and 2011–2021 (n = 140) at a tertiary center in Barcelona.

pmc-12721467.title: Outcomes of respiratory syncytial virus infection in patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease
pmc-12721467.creator: Justine P Enns, Jiaqi Wang, Bohang Jiang, Shruthi Srivatsan, Emily N Kowalski, Xiaosong Wang, Zachary K Williams, Grace Qian, Jennifer Hanberg, Colebrooke Johnson, Madison Negron, Katarina J Bade, Alene Saavedra, Kevin T Mueller, Kathleen MM Vanni, Camille N Kotton, Jeffrey A Sparks, Zachary S Walla
pmc-12721467.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common respiratory viral illness which can cause severe outcomes in older and immunosuppressed populations. There is little data regarding RSV outcomes among people with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs).Methods:This retrospective cohort study examined risk factors for hospitalization in individuals with SARDs and documented RSV infection between 2015 and 2023 at Mass General Brigham (Boston, MA). Clinical data were collected from electronic health records.

pmc-13064886.title: Physics-informed neural network for predicting in vacuo vocal fold eigenmodes: A proof of concept study
pmc-13064886.creator: Mohd Ethar M Al Khasawneh, Michael Döllinger, Zhaoyan Zhang
pmc-13064886.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study investigates a machine-learning approach for real-time computation of in vacuo vocal fold eigenmodes. A physics-informed neural network is trained to predict eigenmodes and eigenfrequencies by integrating the governing equations of vocal fold dynamics. The proposed architecture predicts physically consistent modal shapes and frequency estimates, showing strong agreement with finite-element method results for lower-order modes, achieving mean relative errors below 6% in eigenfrequency prediction and cosine correlation values approaching 1 in eigenmode prediction, while prediction accuracy declines for higher-order modes.

pmc-13255031.title: An advanced reliability reserve incentivizes flexibility investments while safeguarding the electricity market
pmc-13255031.creator: Franziska Klaucke, Karsten Neuhoff, Alexander Roth, Wolf-Peter Schill, Leon Stolle
pmc-13255031.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryTo ensure security of supply in the power sector, many countries are considering capacity mechanisms. Simultaneously, the expansion of variable renewables increases the need for power sector flexibility, with promising options on the demand side. We analyze how a centralized capacity market and an advanced reliability reserve with a moderately high activation price affect demand-side flexibility investments in a German 2030 case study.

pmc-13378028.title: Association Between Radiographic Knee Osteoarthritis, Pre-Fracture Mobility, and Hip Fracture Patterns in Older Adult Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13378028.creator: Süleyman Kaan Öner, Enes Alptekin Canlı, Turan Cihan Dülgeroğlu, Sabit Numan Kuyubaşı, Süleyman Kozlu, Recep Berk Üren
pmc-13378028.description: BackgroundHip fracture morphology in older adults is influenced not only by bone mineral density but also by biomechanical and functional factors. Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) can alter lower-limb alignment, load distribution, and gait patterns, potentially affecting the type of hip fracture sustained.

pmc-13382573.title: Life in the slow lane: reflective practice in postgraduate Emergency Medicine training in South Africa
pmc-13382573.creator: Sian Geraty, Jana Müller
pmc-13382573.description: Emergency Medicine in South Africa faces multiple challenges from insufficient human and physical resources, high patient load, the rapid pace of the profession and the impact of trauma, vicarious trauma and moral injury on physician and trainee wellness. Recently, the College of Emergency Medicine of South Africa introduced wellness as a core competency for an Emergency Medicine specialist.

pmc-13391128.title: Posterior Cervical Fixation: Accuracy and Safety of Free-Hand Inserted Screws
pmc-13391128.creator: Veera Kivistö, Eero Ylipulli, Heikki Mäntymäki, Antti Ronkainen, Juhana Frösen, Tuomo Thesleff
pmc-13391128.description: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES:Posterior fixation of the cervical spine (PFC) is commonly performed with rod-connected screws inserted in the vertebras. Because of the many sensitive structures located adjacent to the vertebras, computer-assisted navigation is often used with PFCs. We assessed safety and efficacy of free-hand placed PFCs.

pmc-13418135.title: Unveiling CTGF and APOA1: key hub genes and therapeutic targets in dilated cardiomyopathy
pmc-13418135.creator: Ran Wang, Jinmeng Chen, Jian Zhu, Xianlin Zhang, Xiaomei Li, Yiyao Jiang, Pingping Jiang
pmc-13418135.description: BackgroundDilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), a life-threatening cardiovascular disease, affects more than 0.04% of the general population. However, the key genes associated with DCM are still unknown.MethodsThree publicly available datasets (GSE120895, GSE53081, and GSE42955) were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database.

pmc-13585857.title: Regulatory Whack-a-mole: A Rapid Scoping Review of Gambling Marketing Restrictions and their (in)Effectiveness
pmc-13585857.creator: Jamie Torrance, Jessica Smith, Alex M. T. Russell, Simon Wright, Leon Y. Xiao, Elen Wyn-Davies, Conor Heath, Philip Newall
pmc-13585857.description: Purpose of ReviewGambling marketing increases participation, spending, and harm. Marketing restrictions represent the best regulatory response. Decades of tobacco and alcohol marketing regulation demonstrate a recurring pattern in which each restriction triggers industry adaptation through, e.g., channel substitution, alibi marketing, and the exploitation of regulatory gaps. However, no review has systematically assessed gambling operator adaptations to marketing restrictions.

uslaw-usc-t21-s364.title: 21 U.S.C. § 364 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t21-s364.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t21-s364.description: United States Code, Title 21 (Food And Drugs); Chapter 9 (Federal Food, Drug, And Cosmetic Act); Subchapter VI (Cosmetics). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this subchapter: (1) Adverse event The term “adverse event” means any health-related event associated with the use of a cosmetic product that is adverse. (2) Cosmetic product The term “cosmetic product” means a preparation of cosmetic ingredients.
